coverage_notes: Swept comprehensively across five major dimensions of agentic UX literature: (1) Agent transparency and explainability in HCI (foundational definitions of legibility/explainability/predictability); (2) Human-in-the-loop control patterns and decision authority (handoff mechanisms, approval workflows, interruption); (3) Trust calibration and reliance dynamics (seminal Lee & See work through recent empirical studies); (4) User mental models and sense-making (how users understand agent behavior and state); (5) Interactive visualization and progress feedback (status visibility, step-by-step execution visibility). Reference-chased from foundational HCI (Shneiderman, Norman, Pirolli, Tufte, Munzner) through recent arXiv papers (2604-2605). Deduplication applied across overlapping search results. Tiered sources: T0 (systematic reviews on automation/HCI), T1 (peer-reviewed CHI/UIST/TOCHI/arXiv), T2 (seminal authors and foundational texts), T3 (high-quality practitioner essays and design system documentation). Notable gaps: limited coverage of agent-specific UI testing frameworks from academic venues; limited work on rollback/state restoration in interrupted workflows; limited formal verification approaches for agent transparency claims.
